> An index is a sorted lookup structure, usually a B-tree, that lets the database jump straight to the rows you asked for instead of reading the whole table.

Put one on the columns you filter and join on, and a query that scanned a million rows can touch a handful. The catch: every index slightly slows writes and uses disk, so you index for the queries you actually run, then use `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` to prove it worked.

Read the full guide: https://www.kloudbean.com/blog/database-indexing-explained/
